input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the new enabled flag is stored on the retry object but only checked inside wraps(), so the direct call, iterator and async paths retry regardless of it
- failure path: Retrying(enabled=False, stop=stop_after_attempt(3))(f) where f raises ValueError: f is called three times and RetryError is raised, identical to enabled=True; only the decorator path honors the flag

Reviewer finding
- description: The enabled flag is only checked by decorator wrappers, so direct calls through Retrying or AsyncRetrying still retry when enabled=False.
- rationale: For example, Retrying(enabled=False, stop=stop_after_attempt(3))(f), where f raises a retryable exception, still executes f three times because the retry controller's __call__ path never checks enabled. Users of the direct controller API therefore cannot disable retries with the newly accepted parameter; the same omission affects iterator-based retry loops.
critique: The finding and the label describe the same defect. In both, the enabled flag is checked only in the decorator/wraps path, so direct __call__, iterator and async controller paths still retry when enabled=False. The finding also gives the same Retrying(enabled=False, stop_after_attempt(3))(f) example.
